chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ismāʿīl al-Mīthamī narrated to us. He said: Ribʿī ibn ʿAbdillāh narrated to us. He said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī ʿAbdillāh said to me:

I said to Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “Is the one who denies this matter, from Banī Hāshim and from others, the same?” So he said to me: “Do not say ‘the denier’; rather say ‘the rejecter,’ from Banī Hāshim and from others.”
Abū al-Ḥasan said: “So I reflected upon it, and I remembered the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, regarding the brothers of Yūsuf:”
“So he recognized them, while they were to him unrecognizing.”

key_terms.الْجَاحِدُ: one who knowingly rejects or repudiates the truth
key_terms.الْمُنْكِرُ: one who does not recognize or acknowledge something
key_terms.هَذَا الْأَمْرِ: this matter, referring in context to the divinely appointed authority

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between someone who does not recognize the truth and someone who knowingly rejects it in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith distinguishes between merely not recognizing something and knowingly rejecting it, especially concerning this matter of authority. The Imam عليه السلام corrects the wording to indicate deliberate rejection, and the narrator supports this distinction through the Qur'anic usage in the story of Yūsuf عليه السلام.
